strapazieren.et: 17th century, from Italian strapazzare (“to handle roughly”). By surface analysis, Strapaze + -ieren.

s: strain, toil, hassle (arduous bodily or mental exertion and distress)
Strapaze.et: 17th century, from Italian strapazzo. The feminine form in -e probably by backformation from the more usual plural; perhaps also influenced by synonyms such as Anstrengung, Mühe, etc.

s: arduous, strenuous, bodily or mentally exhausting

Straps.et: From Low German Strapp (“strap, belt, strand”). Alternatively borrowed from or reinforced by English strap.

s: strap-on (artificial phallus attached with a strap)
